content.text:
This is one axial slice of a T2-weighted fat-suppressed MRI (radiological convention: patient right on image left, anterior at top). It contains a soft-tissue mass.

The left panel is the clean image; the right panel shows numbered marks. Choose the ONE mark that lies inside the tumor, as close to its centre as possible. End your reply with a final line exactly: ANSWER: <mark number>

content.thinking:
Looking at this cross-section, I see two bones with dark rings, suggesting a limb image. The large mass on one side has homogeneous intermediate signal with bright vessels running through it, while the opposite side shows heterogeneous muscle tissue that looks normal — this contrast helps me localize where the tumor is likely arising from.

Checking the numbered marks within that homogeneous region (77, 74, 76, 72, 83, 78, 69), I'm calculating their coordinates and distances from the estimated tumor center around (435, 390). Mark 76 sits closest to center, landing on what looks like a bright vessel-like structure within the mass, so I'll go with that one.

content.text:
The mass appears to be the large, fairly homogeneous intermediate-signal region on the image-left side of the limb, between the two dark bone rings and the right-hand edge of the slice. The heterogeneous muscle-like tissue on the image-right looks like normal tissue.

I estimated the mass spans roughly x 340–525 and y 230–550 in the left panel, putting its centre near (435, 390). Several marks fall inside it (69, 74, 76, 77, 78, 83, 72). Of the marks inside the mass, 76 (about 53 px from the estimated centre) is closest. Mark 74 is about 70 px away and mark 77 about 76 px. Mark 76 sits on a bright linear structure that may be a vessel, but it is still within the mass.

ANSWER: 76
